name: Calcific Tendinopathy of the Shoulder
definition: Deposition of calcium hydroxyapatite within rotator cuff tendons, often the supraspinatus, which may be asymptomatic or cause severe acute/subacute shoulder pain.

typical: Acute severe shoulder pain during resorptive phase

investigations.principle: Plain radiographs often identify calcific deposits.
investigations.MRI: Ultrasound localizes deposits and can guide barbotage; MRI is not always necessary.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs are highly useful for diagnosis.

amber: Ultrasound-guided lavage/barbotage, corticosteroid injection or surgery are options for persistent severe cases.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-shoola/Snayu phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Deposition of calcium hydroxyapatite within rotator cuff tendons, often the supraspinatus, which may be asymptomatic or cause severe acute/subacute shoulder pain.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, locked joint or other listed red flags.
